source_name: Mezha.net English (Bukvy) — Ukraine tech/finance news
why_relevant: English tech-media channel that reliably republishes NBU card-transaction and cash-in-circulation figures with numbers intact; low-friction (no paywall) detection channel for statistic releases.

source_name: Tech.eu — Ukrainian fintech funding coverage
why_relevant: European startup/VC newswire; investor-facing coverage of Ukrainian fintech rounds (e.g. Fintech-IT Group / mono unicorn) with deal terms and investor identities.

source_name: Vestbee — CEE fintech deal insights
why_relevant: CEE VC-ecosystem platform documenting Ukrainian fintech funding rounds and valuations; useful for deal-flow triangulation alongside Tech.eu and InVenture.

source_name: InVenture (English) — Ukrainian M&A and investment news
why_relevant: Ukrainian investment-platform aggregator publishing English deal news and pointing to advisers, funds and transaction parties in banking/fintech — a snowball hub for actor discovery.

source_name: Baker McKenzie newsroom — Ukraine transaction announcements
why_relevant: Law-firm deal announcements confirm the existence, parties and structure of Ukrainian banking/fintech transactions in English before or alongside media coverage; high factual reliability on deal facts.

source_name: UMAEF (U.S. Ukraine-Moldova American Enterprise Fund) newsroom
why_relevant: US government-backed investor publishing first-party English announcements of its Ukrainian financial-sector investments; primary-source for deal facts foreign media then relay.

source_name: GlobalData / ResearchAndMarkets — Ukraine Cards and Payments reports
why_relevant: Commercial market-research series (Opportunities and Risks to 2028/2030) giving card volumes/values, issuer and scheme market shares, and forecasts; the press-release summaries carried by newswires are free and already contain headline figures.

source_name: Euromonitor International — Financial Cards and Payments in Ukraine
why_relevant: Consumer-finance research series (credit cards, debit cards, pre-paid cards in Ukraine) offering channel-level card data; complements GlobalData for triangulating card-issuance and usage estimates.

source_name: 112.ua English edition — payment market structure reporting
why_relevant: Carries structural counts of Ukraine's payment market (payment systems, money-transfer systems, technology operators) in English — useful for participant-landscape mapping.

source_name: Odessa Journal — English business news
why_relevant: Regional English-language Ukrainian outlet with a business desk covering fintech and banking milestones; adds southern-region and shipping/trade-finance angles underreported elsewhere.

source_name: Work.ua — job search (ATM/terminal service engineer queries)
why_relevant: Ukraine's largest general job board; postings for ATM/POS field engineers, acquiring specialists and processing analysts name employers, device fleets, service regions and sometimes vendor stacks (NCR, Diebold, Ingenico, PAX). Aggregate posting counts over time are a proxy for ATM/POS fleet expansion or contraction.

source_name: Robota.ua — company pages and vacancy feeds (payments employers)
why_relevant: Second major UA job board; hosts employer profiles for processing companies (e.g. Ukrainian Processing Center) with headcount signals, office locations and role mixes that reveal which processing/acquiring lines are being staffed up.

source_name: DOU.ua — company vacancy pages (Ukrainian Processing Center / UPC)
why_relevant: DOU is the Ukrainian IT community portal; UPC's vacancy page exposes the technology stack of the country's largest third-party card processor (core processing platform, host interfaces, 3DS, tokenisation, ATM/POS driver work), plus employee reviews and headcount. Tech-stack disclosure here precedes any public announcement of migrations.

source_name: DOU.ua IT events calendar (conference tag)
why_relevant: Aggregator of Ukrainian tech events; a cheap pointer for discovering new fintech/payments conferences, meetups and their agenda pages before they are covered by trade press.

source_name: EMA Association — Payments & Security EMA Conference (agendas, speakers)
why_relevant: The 26-year-running flagship Ukrainian card/payments and anti-fraud conference. Programmes and speaker lists name bank payment executives, processors and fraud volumes; presentations frequently carry transaction and fraud statistics not published elsewhere. Highest-value single conference source for this cell.

source_name: EMA Association — payment market news digest
why_relevant: Recurring 'Новини платіжного ринку від ЄМА' digests aggregate member announcements, project launches and regulatory moves — a snowball pointer to actors and named systems.

source_name: Pay.Forum (FinTech Association of Ukraine) — agenda and speakers
why_relevant: Major payments conference convening bank top management, PSPs, retailers and the NBU Payment Systems Department. Agenda/speaker pages disclose which institutions are driving which payment projects; NBU keynote slots often preview statistics releases.

source_name: NABU (National Association of Banks of Ukraine) — events / Fintech & Payments Forum
why_relevant: Banking association event pages and post-event notes name participating banks and the payment topics they present; NABU also publishes FinAwards retrospectives, linking awards and conferences into one actor map.

source_name: DigitalForum.pro — Fintech & Payments Forum programme and post-event reports
why_relevant: Commercial B2B forum organiser; publishes full agendas, speaker bios and detailed post-event summaries that paraphrase what bank/PSP speakers said about volumes, conversion and infrastructure — quasi-transcripts of otherwise unpublished commentary.

source_name: PaySpace Magazine (psm7.com) — event announcements and coverage
why_relevant: Leading UA fintech trade portal; its event section announces conferences (EMA, Power Payment Summit, Fintech & Payments Forum) with agenda details and speaker names — the fastest single pointer into this cell's conference layer.

source_name: Power Payment Summit: Ukraine–Europe Bridge
why_relevant: Newer summit convening regulators, IFIs, banks, PSPs and payment schemes on Ukraine–EU payment infrastructure convergence (SEPA/EPC). Speaker rosters reveal which institutions are working on cross-border payment integration projects.

source_name: FinAwards (Minfin.com.ua) — nominee lists and winners
why_relevant: Nine-year-running Ukrainian financial-market award. Nominee long-lists are effectively a census of active banks, PSPs, acquirers and fintech apps by category (online acceptance, offline acceptance, fintech tech), and applicant self-descriptions often disclose merchant counts and transaction volumes.

source_name: Finance.ua news — FinAwards category breakdowns (offline/online acquiring providers)
why_relevant: Category-level award coverage identifies the competitive set in offline/online payment acceptance — directly relevant to POS acquiring market structure — and repeats vendor-supplied merchant/transaction figures.

source_name: EasyPay corporate blog — award submissions and self-reported metrics
why_relevant: PSP blog posts campaigning for award votes enumerate the company's nominations, product lines and operating scale — a template case of a vendor disclosing positioning and volumes in an award context.

source_name: National Bank of Ukraine — vacancies page (payment market roles)
why_relevant: NBU job descriptions for payment-systems roles state the regulator's own work programme — oversight of payment system participants, open banking, SEPA alignment, statistics production — and required experience thresholds. A leading indicator of regulatory projects that later generate published statistics.

source_name: PrivatBank careers portal
why_relevant: Largest Ukrainian bank and largest ATM/POS fleet owner. Its vacancies for processing, acquiring, ATM network and card-product roles are the single richest hiring signal about ATM/POS operations and in-house card platform work.

source_name: PUMB (FUIB) careers portal
why_relevant: Top-5 Ukrainian bank with its own careers site; card/acquiring/IT vacancies signal platform projects and regional network staffing.
